name: The Ninth Wall

detectability.signature: A perfectly smooth iridescent membrane returning zero internal data; exterior reads as a soap-bubble shimmer with a hard quantum-noise floor

proximity: Starlight warps smoothly around the bubble, painting a false sky on its far side
Instruments report the bubble's surface as simultaneously nearer and farther than optics allow
contact: The membrane admits matter selectively; hull sections pass while loose objects rebound as if from glass
Interior physics diverge subtly: combustion burns cooler, clocks lose milliseconds per minute
prolonged_exposure: Divergent physics accumulate; unshielded electronics desynchronize from outside timekeeping entirely
Organisms adapted to the bubble cannot survive readmission to normal space without gradual acclimation

behavior.cycle: Radius shrinks 11 meters per year on a precisely linear schedule

phenomena: Impossible geometries visible within: interior structures seen from outside occupy impossible perspectives
Light bending around the bubble creating a lens-like false horizon
Subspace interference patterns ringing the membrane like ripples around a drumhead
hazards: Entrapment as the contracting wall eventually reaches any object adrift inside
Reality breakdown at the membrane interface for matter that resists admission
Complete life support compromise once interior atmosphere chemistry drifts past survivable margins
opportunities: Access to otherwise unreachable regions: the bubble's interior preserves artifacts of its builders intact
Archaeological significance beyond estimate; the only known surviving structure of the Waning Artificers
Test exotic theories under controlled divergent physics, a physicist's sealed experiment billions of credits in the making
known_incidents: The boarding team of the cruiser Halberd's Oath entered in 2416; three returned after six hours describing 'a city that agreed to be seen,' while two remained voluntarily and are presumed dead as the wall closed
Salvage magnate Corin Ashe offered 40 million credits for a hull section of the interior city; no claimant has ever collected
description: The Ninth Wall hangs in vacuum as a flawless iridescent sphere fifteen thousand kilometers across, so smooth that sensors can find no feature to range against. Light slides around it and paints a plausible continuation of the starfield on its far side, so unwary pilots have been known to fly straight at what looks like open sky. Through the membrane, glimpses of interior structures resolve at angles no perspective can justify, towers seen simultaneously from above and below.

Unlike nearly everything else in the anomaly registries, the Wall is punctual. Its radius contracts by exactly eleven meters per year, a figure refined across decades of measurement to five decimal places, and its surface physics never waver. Matter seeking entry is judged piece by piece: hulls pass, loose tools bounce off as though the air itself turned to glass, and inside, fire burns cooler and every clock runs a few milliseconds slow.

Scholars attribute the bubble to the Waning Artificers, a civilization that vanished nine centuries ago leaving this as their sole intact work, a museum sealed in its own physics. In 2416 the cruiser Halberd's Oath sent a team inside, and the three who came back spoke of a preserved city that seemed to permit observation on its own terms. Two of their crewmates refused extraction; the wall has since advanced well past the point where rescue would be arithmetic rather than hope.

The contraction schedule is public knowledge, which lends the site a quiet urgency: at current rate, the interior city has roughly six centuries before the wall arrives. Archaeologists, physicists, and salvage interests circle one another in a treaty zone on the boundary, each forbidden from what the others want most. Every expedition brief ends with the same warning the Halberd's survivors gave: the Wall decides what enters, and it has never once explained itself.
